_comment: Case configuration template of the river-cross-sections skill. Values '<ASK>' or '<FIND>' must be filled before the scripts that read them are run: '<FIND>' = look for it in the case material (layers, docs, model files), '<ASK>' = ask the user (see references/kickoff.md). All paths are relative to the folder of this file (the working folder). Numeric defaults are the values used on the Brenta; keep or change them with the user. Every key is described in references/config.md.

fields._comment: logical name -> field name. Input layers: <FIND> from the layers. Derived layers: keep these defaults (Brenta names) or ask the user for a naming convention.

face_classes._comment: class of a planar-graph face from the name of its region point; first matching class in 'order' wins.
face_classes._todo: fill names/prefix/suffix from the region-point names of the case (<FIND>, then confirm with the user); fixed / editable / fixed_bank_names <ASK>

locked._comment: breaklines bounding regions with these mat_id (walls) are never modified; locked_lines.py writes their fids.
locked._todo: <ASK> mat_id of regions whose lines are never touched (e.g. walls); [] if none

originals._comment: region points of the original layer (fid <= region_fid_max) are never moved; fids expected to be missing in the derived layer (replaced or deleted with the user's consent).
originals.region_fid_max: <FIND> (largest fid of the original region-point layer)

nodestrings._comment: boundary-condition lines and other non-section nodestrings

exceptions._comment: accepted by the user; every entry needs a reason and a date. A pair is excluded if either section is listed.

bank._comment: bankpoint search rule; distances in metres, heights in metres (DTM units)

check_bp._comment: sec_in = bankpoint-computation input in the work folder; stream_prefix maps the tag (or stream) of a sec_in record to the section-name prefix; kind_* = bankpoint kind values; the numbers repeat the limit rule of the bankpoint computation (bank.py): window = min(cap, mid-width+mid_window), or toe+toe_window if the bed is wider than wide_bed or the window is shorter than min_window beyond the toe.

check_geom._comment: fids of the derived breaklines excluded from the crossing comparison (those handled by the fix_near_nodes special cases)

fix_near_nodes._comment: special cases are Brenta-specific breaklines (fids of the derived breakline layer). laid_on_section: a breakline lying exactly on the section (its ends slide to the crossings of the section with their host toe lines). source_strip: upstream breakline laid on the section, downstream one slid to rules.near_node (radius + slide_margin) from the crossings.

fix_bridges._comment: tol: a breakline vertex closer than this (m) to the nodestring is 'on' it; min_overlap: length (m) of a breakline along a nodestring that makes a pair; max_shift: acceptance limit on the displacement (m); nodestring_regex: only nodestrings with a matching name are examined (null = all); exclude: pairs [breakline fid, nodestring] found by the detection but deliberately not fixed.

next_bed._comment: distances in metres along the section normal

obst._comment: distances in metres along the section normal

prep_write._comment: centerline_sources: per reach code, the source line the centerline is cut from. file = GeoPackage relative to the working folder; line = name in the centerline name field; start = 'zero' or 'first_section_s_asta' (chainage of the first section of the reach on the source line); end = 'last_section_s' (chainage of the last section) or 'line_end'; s0_from_start = write the start chainage as s0 (else null).

<reach code>.file: <layer with the source centerline, relative to the working folder>

regions2._comment: preserved_pairs: faces that already hold exactly these region point fids (pre-existing pair in the original data) are left as they are; report_points: fids whose status is printed

sections_csv._comment: titles of the 14 CSV columns, in order: section, reach, chainage, then left z/dist_cp/kind/rule/prom, right z/dist_cp/kind/rule/prom, section length

verify3._comment: kinds = allowed bankpoint kind values; kind_max/kind_wall = kind names of the DTM-maximum and wall bankpoints (kind_wall is also its rule value); prom_min = minimum prominence (m) of a kind_max bankpoint; notes = optional text appended to three check lines (history of the accepted differences in this case).

widen._comment: cltab_alias: config centerline name -> key of cltab.pkl, for tables written with other keys (the Brenta cl2.py used 'main'/'vecchio'). ray_range: half length of the normal; station_radius: a top vertex takes the shift of the nearest top station within this distance; min_shift: smaller shifts are ignored; oblique_cos: forced T vertices slide along the incident line when its cosine with the normal exceeds this.

placement._comment: place.py / dp.py / export_sec.py / assemble.py. Weights: the cost of a candidate section is the sum of boundary*hitB + inner*hitO + obstacle (crossing a section of an earlier reach) + near*(toe crossings closer than rules.near_node.radius to a toe vertex) + xn*(toe crossings closer than that radius to a meeting point of nodestring and breakline) + angle*(crossings sharper than rules.min_angle_deg) + perp*(deviation in degrees from the perpendicular of the longer chord); a step costs step*(distance - spacing)^2 and, if the chord between two centre points is outside spacing +- tol, chord_base + chord*|chord - spacing|; invalid = candidate without toe/top on both sides or in a keep-clear zone.

assemble._comment: side_overrides: the bankpoint of one side of a section is replaced by the one computed for a pseudo-section (files relative to the working folder; first record used). Brenta: N16050 is extended to the right channel.

widening._comment: zones: first matching zone wins (s_from <= s <= s_to along the 1 m centerline of cltab.pkl, s_to null = no limit). mode 'corridor': top-to-top width >= min, shift split symmetrically; mode 'bank': each bank, toe to top, >= min. check_min (optional) = limit used by check_widen.py (default min). Distances in metres.
